meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Owen saw his zero on his phone in class. Who decided on it?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now show me what you have.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing those down. Pasting from another file isn't a crime. Did anyone ask Owen before the zero?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays quiet. And you still haven't told me whether Owen was heard before you entered that zero.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare every day, Hale. A wrong line is a wrong line.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. So what are you putting on the table?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
People change their minds in two weeks. I asked what you're proposing.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, in writing tonight. Whether anyone heard Owen before that zero goes in the same email.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
I'll ask him tonight. Nothing is booked until your email is in my inbox.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, after school and not in front of his class, before December 1, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require that commitment in writing, along with a direct answer on whether anyone heard Owen before the zero was entered. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Her last position, accepting a private supervised rewrite under 4.4 once it arrives in writing, though she still wants your email and an answer on whether Owen was heard before the zero, and that rewrite with nothing on his record is the fair outcome.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times, which was dated, tied to his own file and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: You never answered her question about whether Owen was heard before the zero, so she would not book the rewrite in the room.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on the night before it was due, very close to that kind of late night, and while it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: The first time she asked whether Owen was heard before the zero, answer it plainly in one sentence before turning to the misquoted line.
